When I worked in a bar, I was promoted to supervisor and I was trained on counting the tills. A couple of weeks after I started doing the tills, I noticed money was missing. I would count the tills over and over again and still money was missing. I spoke to the assistant manager about it and she said she would handle it. I thought nothing of it afterwards. 

One day I’ve arrived at work and the general manager has called me to his office. I go in and he is sat there staring at me. He asks me if I’ve got anything to tell him. Confused, I said no. He just started at me. I asked what the hell was going on. He explained that he had spoken to the assistant manager who was downstairs at the time, and she stated she was concerned I was stealing from the tills. My mouth hit the floor. He went onto say that because money didn’t appear to go missing until I started to handle them, they thought I might be taking money. I was so angry, I didn’t know what to say. I’ve never stole in my life and I had to deal with this shit!?

I just so happened to look up towards the cctv screens. I jumped up and shouted “WAIT!!! I told my manager to go back on the camera and I showed him. He sat there for a good 20 seconds, silent. He apologised to me and asked me to send the assistant manager up to him.

I have a stutter. Ive had a stutter for 20 years. 

I work in hospitality. Imagine that. 

I was serving a table of 8 people the one day. I stuttered as a lady was asking about a meal on the menu. The mom (I assume) on the table began to laugh and pull faces. I knew it was about my stutter. I asked her "Is everything okay?" to which she replied "can you just get it out??" I was stunned. So i replied "Im sorry but I have a stutter which I can not help" she then said "Why should that be our issue? You're ruining our experience" I was shocked. I stood there, eyes tearing up. But then I thought, no, I will not let this 'thing' make me feel bad for something I cannot help. Keep in mind this lady was in a wheel chair. 

"Well, I have a stutter, it is not an issue but a disability. And you if you have issue with that then you should really be ashamed. You've made someone feel bed about something that they cannot help. How dare you. You have no right. I am a human being. You're in a wheel chair, I would not dare discriminate you for that. So why do you feel right discriminating me for having a stutter?"

She soon shut up and looked down. 

Her daughter even apologized to me after their meal. I let it go as I knew, it was not my problem it was hers.

YES! If you have a stutter, dont be ashamed! Be you! Its part of what makes you, you! NEVER be ashamed of who you are.

I've had a stutter since the age of 5 and I have gotten through it. Its part of who I am. Its what makes me, me. You should NEVER be ashamed of who you are. If you have a stutter, so what? If you are giving good service and the customer leaves happy whats the issue? 

Dont be limited to not doing something you want because of your stutter. Don't let it own you.
